item.title: NPA boss seeks regional port cooperation to cut cargo costs
item.description: By Godwin Oritse President of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has called for stronger regional cooperation among ports to reduce cargo clearance delays, lower logistics costs and boost intra-African trade. Dantsoho, who is also Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), made the call at the association’s 46th Annual Council and Joint Gulf of Guinea Commission-PMAWCA Forum in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea. He urged port authorities to prioritise strategic collaboration over unhealthy competition, identifying prolonged cargo dwell time, high port charges, expensive transport corridors and poor interoperability among customs systems as major obstacles to regional trade. He noted that the challenges particularly affected landlocked countries, including Mali, Niger, Chad and Burkina Faso, which depend on coastal ports for international trade. Dantsoho also identified geopolitical disruptions, climate change, cyber threats and emerging maritime decarbonisation regulations as challenges requiring urgent collective action by regional port authorities. He called for increased investment in modern port infrastructure, digital security, green port initiatives and the blue economy, including ship repair, sustainable fishing and clean marine fuels. Warning against the implications of failing to adapt to changing global shipping regulations, he said the energy transition could reshape international shipping routes and port calls. “Moreover, the maritime decarbonisation regulations currently taking shape at the International Maritime Organization will soon redraw global shipping routes and ports of call: any port that fails to prepare for this energy transition risks being bypassed altogether. “Finally, rapid digitalisation, while indispensable, exposes our operations to sophisticated cyber threats that we can no longer afford to underestimate,” he said. The PMAWCA president urged member ports to develop clear implementation roadmaps and strengthen accountability, proposing that progress on agreed resolutions be presented at the association’s 47th Annual Council. Also speaking, Executive Secretary of the Gulf of Guinea Commission, Mr Jose Mba Abeso, called for stronger maritime security cooperation to combat illegal fishing, drug and human trafficking, as well as protect critical offshore infrastructure, including subsea cables and gas pipelines. Similarly, Equatorial Guinea’s Minister of Environment and Blue Economy, Mr Fidel Esono Mba Eyono, stressed the importance of sustainable exploitation of marine resources, warning against pollution, illegal fishing and other activities threatening marine ecosystems. The post NPA boss seeks regional port cooperation to cut cargo costs appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC debunks claims of remote BVAS log-out, result loss
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed claims that its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) can be remotely logged out before voting concludes. The commission described the claims as false and misleading in a clarification issued on Tuesday through its official X account. INEC was responding to a viral Instagram video alleging that officials could remotely log out voters from BVAS before voting ended. The commission described the video as fabricated and misleading, urging Nigerians to disregard its claims about the system’s operation. “For the avoidance of doubt, the commission wishes to clarify the operational procedures of the BVAS and the process for uploading polling unit results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV),” it stated. According to INEC, each polling unit receives unique login credentials, which are issued to the presiding officer on the eve of an election. The credentials enable the official to access BVAS for voter accreditation and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet after voting. “The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated. It explained that only the poll official operating the device could log in or log out during accreditation or result uploading. “There is no provision for remote log-out by any external individual or authority,” INEC added. The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost. It said the IReV application was upgraded after the 2023 general election to incorporate an offline uploading capability. INEC recalled that some election officials were held hostage at polling units during the 2023 elections because poor connectivity prevented result uploads. It explained that the upgrade allows officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload results offline before stakeholders. “The uploaded result sheet remains securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission,” the commission stated. It added that results were automatically transmitted to IReV once the device regained internet connectivity. This happens as officials proceed from their polling units to ward collation centres, without requiring further manual intervention. INEC assured Nigerians that BVAS and IReV operate under established procedures designed to protect electoral integrity, transparency and credibility. It urged the public to disregard the viral video and avoid creating or sharing unverified information. The commission advised Nigerians to rely exclusively on its official communication channels for accurate information. “INEC remains committed to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections,” it stated. The post INEC debunks claims of remote BVAS log-out, result loss appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Pension fund assets hit N31.8trn, as 350,000 Nigerians join scheme
item.description: By Rosemary Iwunze Nigeria’s pension industry recorded an asset growth of more than N4 trillion in eight months to August 2026, as total assets under management stood at N31.8 trillion by August 2026. The sharp increase was buoyed by strong equity market performance, investment returns as well as increase in the number of contributors, with approximately 350,000 new Retirement Savings Account (RSA) registrations recorded during the period. The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer, CEO, of the Pension Fund Operators Association of Nigeria, PenOp, Mrs. Anthonia Ifeanyi-Okoro, disclosed this yesterday during the 2026 Annual Media Retreat held virtually. According to her, the continuous increase in subscriber base is attributable to increased awareness and enforcement of the scheme in both public and private sectors of the nation’s economy. Ifeanyi-Okoro said: “Pension assets under management had climbed to N31.8 trillion as of August 2026, reflecting the industry’s strongest growth momentum in recent years and reinforcing its expanding role in Nigeria’s financial system. “The industry also recorded growth in its membership base, with approximately 11.3 million RSA holders, as efforts to deepen pension participation and strengthen retirement savings continued.” Ifeanyi-Okoro attributed the expansion to improved investment performance, increased contributor enrollment and the gradual diversification of pension fund portfolios. She noted that the equities market recorded a bullish performance during the first two quarters of 2026, contributing positively to pension fund returns. Also speaking, Head of Branding and Communications of PenOp’s Executive Committee, Adeola Oyegbade, identified the performance of the equities market and the entry of new contributors as important drivers of pension asset growth. She disclosed that, approximately, 350,000 Nigerians registered under the pension scheme during the period, adding that, the increase in contributors complemented investment returns in driving the industry’s asset expansion. Oyegbade also explained that the industry’s declining exposure to Federal Government securities was part of a deliberate investment diversification strategy and should not be interpreted as a loss of confidence in government instruments. Ifeanyi-Okoro had earlier disclosed that pension fund allocation to Federal Government securities declined from about 65 per cent at the end of 2025 to 55.9 per cent as of August 2026, as operators increased exposure to other investment opportunities. item.title: YPP presidential hopeful unveils plan to cut governance cost
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arc. Peter Agada, has unveiled a governance model, tagged LabourDirect, which he said would reduce the cost of governance through direct labour, lower infrastructure costs and the elimination of contract inflation and financial leakages. Agada unveiled the initiative on Tuesday during the flag-off of his presidential campaign and the presentation of his manifesto in Abuja. Describing LabourDirect as the centrepiece of his proposed administration, he said it was designed to replace inflated contracts with a more transparent and cost-effective system of delivering public infrastructure. He said, “Today, we do not just launch a campaign. We launch a movement, we flag off a new Nigeria. “I stand before you to unveil my manifesto. Not a manifesto of promises. A manifesto of numbers. A manifesto of infrastructure. A manifesto of accountability. My manifesto is called LabourDirect.” The YPP candidate identified the high cost of governance as a major factor contributing to Nigeria’s economic challenges, arguing that excessive spending on roads, buildings, electricity and water infrastructure leaves insufficient resources for education, healthcare and job creation. He said Nigeria’s population, currently estimated at approximately 245 million, was projected to rise to 305 million in 10 years and 365 million in 20 years. Agada also put the country’s Gross Domestic Product at $386.67 billion, while claiming that 154 million Nigerians, representing 63 per cent of the population, were living in multidimensional poverty. “We are growing, but we are getting poorer. This is a jobless boom,” he said. On the country’s debt burden, Agada said public debt stood at ₦166.79 trillion as of June 30, 2026, while debt servicing consumed ₦15.52 trillion, representing 45.2 per cent of government revenue. He argued that the amount spent servicing debt had significantly reduced the resources available for critical public services. “We spend ₦15.52 trillion, 45.2 per cent of all our revenue, just to service debt. Almost half of everything we earn goes to pay old debts. That is why we have no money for schools, hospitals, and roads,” he said. Explaining the LabourDirect model, Agada said it would eliminate unnecessary intermediaries, ghost workers and inflated contracts, thereby reducing the cost of executing government projects. Using road construction as an example, he claimed that while the government spends about ₦2.5 billion to construct one kilometre of road, his model could deliver the same distance for between ₦375 million and ₦500 million. “I stand here today on a road that I built. Not with government money. Not with a loan. With LabourDirect. “The government standard rate for a road like this is ₦2.5 billion per kilometre. I built this road for a fraction of that,” he said. item.title: FG targets $9.3bn care economy, woos private investors
item.description: IFC push investment as Lagos develops care policy framework By Peter Egwuatu The Federal Government is targeting a $9.3 billion care economy as it moves to attract private sector investment into childcare, elderly care and disability support services. The initiative follows the Federal Executive Council’s approval of the National Care Policy and Implementation Plan 2026–2030, aimed at transforming the sector into an organised industry capable of creating millions of jobs and increasing women’s participation in the economy. Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Suleiman-Ibrahim, disclosed this yesterday in Lagos at the National Care Economy Forum hosted by the World Bank Group. She was represented by the Director, Child Development Department, Ali Andrew Maduga. “Our task is to move beyond recognising care as a social responsibility to establishing it as an organised, productive and investable component of Nigeria’s economy,” she said. She disclosed that the Council, on October 28, 2026, also directed the Ministers of Justice and Women Affairs to develop an executive bill to provide legislative backing for the policy. Citing UN Women’s 2026 care economy modelling, she said closing unpaid care gaps and expanding universal childcare could contribute at least $9.3 billion to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product and generate between 9.4 million and 17 million jobs. She added that caregiving responsibilities accounted for 20.16 per cent of women’s withdrawal from the labour force, compared with 0.6 per cent for men. Earlier, Head of Office, Nigeria, International Finance Corporation (IFC), Christian Mulamula, described care as economic infrastructure rather than merely a family responsibility. “Care may begin at home, but its impact does not end at the front door. It shapes whether people, particularly women, can take up opportunities and participate fully in the economy. “Care is economic infrastructure,” he said. He disclosed that 92 per cent of childcare facilities were small, independently owned businesses, while 76 per cent of childcare entrepreneurs lacked access to formal finance. “Investing in childcare is about freeing talent and productivity into the economy while giving children a strong start in life,” he added. Meanwhile, Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Abayomi Oluyomi, said the state was developing an investment-oriented care policy framework. “We want a care economy in which families can access reliable and affordable services, care providers can operate viable businesses, and those who work in the sector can earn decent livelihoods under appropriate professional standards,” he said. Sanwo-Olu urged financial institutions, employers and private investors to support the sector, noting that government funding alone could not provide the required facilities and services. item.title: FG moves to strengthen foreign missions, boost economic diplomacy
item.description: By Favour Ulebor ABUJA—The Federal Government has announced plans to strengthen Nigeria’s foreign missions, improve consular services and make diplomacy more focused on attracting investment, promoting trade and supporting economic growth. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, disclosed this in a statement, yesterday, by his Special Assistant on Digital Media and Public Diplomacy, Raphael Oni, following the opening of the sixth Foreign Policy School (FPS-6) in Abuja. The programme, organised by the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs, NIIA, and the Peace-Building Development Consult, PBDC, is being held from November 16 to 18, 2026, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Tafawa Balewa House, Abuja. The event, themed “Foreign Policy as a Tool for National Security and Economic Growth,” focuses on how Nigeria can use diplomacy to strengthen national security, attract economic opportunities and promote its interests internationally. Speaking at the opening ceremony, Enikanolaiye said Nigeria’s foreign policy must be built on a strong domestic foundation to achieve meaningful results abroad. He explained that the administration of President Bola Tinubu was introducing reforms within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to improve its operations and ensure that Nigerian missions abroad delivered measurable results. According to him, the government’s foreign policy is guided by the four Ds: Demography, development, diaspora and democracy, with the welfare and interests of Nigerians at the centre. He noted that the approach didn’t reduce Africa’s importance in Nigeria’s foreign policy but recognised that the country must strengthen its economy and institutions to play a more effective role on the continent. The minister recalled that the ministry adopted the motto “Nigeria First” in 2007, adding that the present administration was working to give it practical meaning. He said Nigerian missions abroad would be repositioned as centres for trade, investment and technology partnerships, while also improving consular services for citizens living overseas. He said: “We are moving beyond the mantra of diplomacy for diplomacy’s sake to a purposeful engagement calibrated to serve our people.” Enikanolaiye also announced three measures to improve accountability and performance across Nigerian missions. He identified them as the Stations Charter, which assigns specific priorities to each mission; SCAPER, an annual performance assessment for Heads of Mission; and the Global Best Practices Project, which will enable missions identify successful policies and practices that could benefit Nigeria. He explained that the measures would ensure that diplomatic activities produced practical results rather than focus only on meetings and engagements. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 18, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened trading on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, with the gap between the two segments widening further. At the official window, data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows that the naira closed the previous session on Tuesday, November 17, at a volume-weighted NFEM rate of ₦1,358.09 per dollar. During Tuesday’s official trading session, the local currency opened at ₦1,355.80 per dollar and fluctuated between an intraday high of ₦1,354.00 and a low of ₦1,364.50 before settling at ₦1,363.00 at the close. Meanwhile, live international interbank spot tracking early Wednesday morning hovered around ₦1,351.25 per dollar. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira traded significantly weaker. Street dealers and Bureau de Change (BDC) operators in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at an average of ₦1,440 per dollar early Wednesday morning, with buying and selling rates ranging between ₦1,435 and ₦1,445 per dollar. Based on the latest official NFEM rate of ₦1,358.09 and the parallel market average of ₦1,440.00, the spread between the official and unofficial markets currently stands at approximately ₦81.91 per dollar. Market analysts note that the persistent divergence between both windows reflects heightened seasonal import demand, corporate foreign exchange obligations, and a slowdown in autonomous dollar inflows. Recent market intelligence indicates that while Nigeria’s external reserves slipped slightly by roughly $390 million from their late-October peak of $55.26 billion due to central bank market interventions, the reserve buffer remains over 26 percent higher than the $43.54 billion recorded during the same period in 2025. Financial analysts expect the Central Bank of Nigeria to maintain liquidity support in the official NFEM window to keep official rates anchored near the ₦1,350 to ₦1,365 band, even as retail and unfulfilled demand continues to exert upward pressure on parallel market quotes. item.title: Atiku, Barau, Ikeja LG boss mourn Vanguard Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: By Henry Umoru & Olasunkanmi Akoni ABUJA — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, and Chairman of Ikeja Local Government Area of Lagos State, Akeem Dauda, have mourned the death of Vanguard Newspapers’ Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Ajasa. Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), after a brief illness. He was aged 44. His death was announced by the management of Vanguard Media Limited, publishers of Vanguard Newspapers. In a condolence message posted on his X handle on Tuesday, Atiku described Ajasa’s death as a painful loss to the journalism profession and Vanguard Media Limited. The African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate said the late editor’s death was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short. He said, “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed. “His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.” Atiku extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and the deceased’s family, friends and colleagues. He prayed that the memories Ajasa left behind would comfort his loved ones and that God would grant them the strength to bear the loss. Similarly, Senator Barau described Ajasa as a thoroughbred professional and one of the finest minds in Nigeria’s digital journalism space. In a condolence message issued by his spokesperson, Ismail Mudashir, the Deputy Senate President said Ajasa’s dedication to truth and accuracy distinguished him in the profession. He said, “Femi Ajasa’s dedication and commitment to truth and accuracy set him apart and distinguished him among others. His death is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family, the Vanguard family, but to the entire Nigerian media industry.” Barau recalled that Ajasa began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror in 2012 before working with TheNewsGuru and Pulse. He later returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position in which he distinguished himself through professionalism and commitment to the journalism profession. The senator extended his condolences to the Ajasa family of Ajido, Badagry, Lagos State, the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the journalism union, friends and professional associates of the deceased. He prayed that God would grant the bereaved family, colleagues and loved ones the strength to bear the loss and grant the deceased eternal rest. Also mourning, Ikeja Local Government Chairman, Akeem Dauda, described Ajasa’s death as a painful loss to the media industry and the journalism profession. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 18 – An M-class Solar Flare
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 18 – An… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Medium-Sized Solar Flare Explanation: What a flare for the chromatic ! Today’s image captures a piece of the Sun ’s chromosphere , the layer of the Sun ’s atmosphere above its surface where the temperature rises . Why would the Sun become hotter farther away from its core ? This is potentially due to energy from the swirling magnetic fields extending up through the Sun’s atmosphere. Those same magnetic fields can twist and snap , releasing light and energetic particles as a solar flare . The H-alpha filter used for today’s image captures light from energized hydrogen atoms as they travel off the Sun’s surface during a flare on May 14, 2025. This flare was classified as an M1 based on GOES observations , meaning it was moderately bright in X-rays . M-class flares can cause radio blackouts at Earth’s poles and minor radiation storms that can harm astronauts. They aren’t even the most powerful flares ! NASA, NOAA , and other agencies monitor the Sun to predict and identify such storms so we can protect humans on Earth and in space. item.title: Oil production rises 6.2% to 1.615m bpd, Dangote supply jumps 25%
item.description: •Pipeline outages, terminal delays hamper output By Ediri Ejoh Nigeria’s average daily crude oil and condensate production rose by 6.2 per cent to 1.615 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025, from 1.521 million bpd in 2024, while crude oil supplied to Dangote Refinery increased by 25.3 per cent to 94.44 million barrels. The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) disclosed this in its 2025 Financial and Operational Performance Report, released at the weekend. The report showed that crude oil production, excluding condensates, increased by 12.6 per cent to 1.475 million bpd in 2025, from 1.310 million bpd in the preceding year. Companies operating under Joint Venture (JV) arrangements and those in land terrains accounted for the largest shares of national production. A breakdown of monthly output showed that production peaked at 1.701 million bpd in July and 1.688 million bpd in June, while the lowest output of 1.521 million bpd was recorded in December. Providing details of production performance, the commission stated: “Reconciled crude oil produced was 589,600,527 barrels (538,696,941 barrels of oil and 50,903,586 barrels of condensate). The daily average production figure was 1,615,344 barrels per day (1,475,882 barrels of oil per day and 139,462 barrels of condensate per day).” It also disclosed that 48 Field Development Plans (FDPs) were approved during the year to develop about 1,751.15 million stock tank barrels of oil reserves, 104.48 million stock tank barrels of condensate reserves and 8.19 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves. However, pipeline outages, planned maintenance and terminal operational challenges constrained production during the year. The commission identified the Trans-Niger Pipeline (TNP), Nembe Creek Trunk Line (NCTL) and Trans Forcados Pipeline (TFP) among the major pipelines affected by outages. “The most prevalent cause during the year was outages of key pipelines (TNP, NCTL, and TFP),” the report stated. It added that “planned maintenance and vessel/tanker loading delays at terminals, which led to the shut-in of wells, also contributed significantly to the deferred volumes.” Meanwhile, crude oil supplied to Dangote Refinery rose to 94.436 million barrels in 2025, from 75.391 million barrels in 2024, representing an increase of 25.3 per cent. In a related development, the NUPRC last week reported that Nigeria’s average daily crude oil and condensate production declined by 1.7 per cent to 1.68 million bpd in October 2026, from 1.71 million bpd in September. Despite the decline, Nigeria met its Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) crude oil production quota for the sixth consecutive month. Crude oil output, excluding condensates, averaged 1.51 million bpd, representing 101 per cent of the country’s 1.5 million bpd quota. item.title: Sierra Snow Season Spins Up
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Sierra Snow Season Spins Up Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search November 12 November 14 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison November 12 November 14 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison November 12 November 14 Curtain Toggle 2-Up California’s Sierra Nevada got an early taste of wintry weather when one of the first major snowfalls of the water year arrived on November 13, 2026. A moisture-laden storm delivered heavy rains to lower elevations in the Sacramento area and snow accumulations of around a foot to some mountainous areas. The recent bout of wet weather was the first in a quick succession of Pacific storms bringing rain, snow, and wind to the U.S. West in mid-November. The MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Terra satellite captured this image (right) of fresh snow in the Sierra Nevada on the morning of November 14, during a lull between weather systems. Two days earlier (left), the mountains were mostly bare, with snow appearing only at the highest elevations. Nearly 12 inches (30 centimeters) of snow fell at Donner Pass, northwest of Lake Tahoe, on November 13, according to the Central Sierra Snow Laboratory . The accumulation snarled traffic on Interstate 80 in the area, prompting officials to close the highway in both directions that evening. To the south, the ski resort at Mammoth Mountain reported 9 to 13 inches (23 to 33 centimeters) of new snow, and officials at Yosemite National Park closed several roads ahead of the storm. More wet weather and mountain snow are forecast to follow . The National Weather Service (NWS) issued a winter storm warning for portions of the Sierras above 5,000 feet (1,500 meters) in elevation from November 18 to 20. NWS warned of difficult-to-impossible travel conditions, gusty winds, and snow accumulations of around 4 feet (120 centimeters) possible above 8,000 feet (2,400 meters). item.title: 66 Years Later, William Shatner's Forgotten 'Twilight Zone' Is Still a Haunting Masterpiece
item.description: “Nightmare at 20,000 Feet” is one of the all-time great episodes of The Twilight Zone . Starring William Shatner, the story is about a man who is taking his first flight after having had a nervous breakdown. During the flight, he looks out the window and sees a creature, called a gremlin, on the wing that taunts him and tears apart pieces of the plane. No one can see the gremlin but him, and even his own wife attributes it to his fragile mental state. The story is a brilliant commentary on paranoia and Shatner was captivating in the role. It was so good that it sometimes overshadows Shatner’s other great episode of The Twilight Zone , which premiered 66 years ago today.

item.title: APC shuts down Umuahia for Tinubu
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The All Progressives Congress, APC, on Monday, shut down Umuahia, the Abia State capital, as it formally flagged off its campaign for the 2027 general elections, with a massive rally that drew party leaders, candidates and supporters from across the state. The Umuahia Township Stadium, venue of the rally, was filled to capacity, while heavy vehicular and human traffic disrupted movement around adjoining streets as thousands of party faithful struggled to access the venue. Leading the charge, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, declared that Abia would deliver 75 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in 2027, insisting that the President would not have to beg for the constitutionally required 25 per cent in the state. Kalu said APC had about 162,000 members in Abia and that the party had challenged each member to mobilise 10 additional voters for Tinubu. According to him, such mobilisation would translate into over 1.6 million votes for the President. “Don’t beg for 25 per cent. Your sons and daughters in Abia State will give you 75 per cent. We have about 2.3 million voters in Abia State. We are mobilising. We are not sleeping,” he declared. He challenged those questioning APC’s electoral strength in Abia to wait for the party’s planned rally at Enyimba Stadium, Aba, on December 7, insisting that the Umuahia rally, organised within one week, was only a foretaste of what was coming. Tinubu has remembered South-East — Kalu Explaining why the South-East should support Tinubu’s second-term ambition, Kalu listed the establishment of the South-East Development Commission, stabilisation of the foreign exchange market, student loans under NELFUND, tax reforms and increased security funding among the administration’s achievements. He said the President had demonstrated commitment to the region by addressing longstanding grievances dating back to the Nigerian Civil War. Kalu, who acknowledged the contributions of the President to the establishment of the SEDC, said the commission’s interventions would soon begin to translate into visible development across the five South-East states. He also commended the President for supporting his emergence as Deputy Speaker, describing the position as an opportunity to advance the interests of the region. item.title: Car washer steals customer’s SUV
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—A 36-year-old car washer, Pius, has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment for stealing a customer’s Toyota Lexus 330 SUV in Enugu State. The Enugu State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Daniel Ndukwe. According to the statement, Pius stole the black Lexus SUV on November 5, 2026, after it was entrusted to him by its owner for washing at Fourth Dimension, Enugu. Rather than wash and return the vehicle, the convict, a native of Ugep in Yakurr Local Government Area of Cross River State, allegedly absconded with it and fled to his hometown. Following a complaint by the vehicle’s owner, operatives of the New Haven Police Division deployed technical intelligence to track down and arrest him in Cross River State. The stolen SUV was subsequently recovered on November 11, 2026. The police said Pius was arraigned before the Enugu North Magistrate Court on November 16, 2026, on a one-count charge of stealing. He pleaded guilty to the charge and was convicted and sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment by the court. The Command commended the operatives involved in the investigation and arrest, as well as the court for the speedy dispensation of justice. It reiterated its commitment to sustaining efforts to rid Enugu State of criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents and their property. item.title: Court adjourns divorce case of Gov Yusuf, wife to Dec 15
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – An Upper Area Court sitting in the Gudu District of Abuja, yesterday, fixed December 15, to hear the divorce case involving Governor Abba Yusuf of Kano State and his estranged wife, Zainab. Trial judge, Ado Muktar, deferred hearing of the suit, to enable the parties to file and exchange the necessary processes. While the Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, appeared for the governor, the plaintiff, Zainab, was represented by her lawyer, Aliyu Baba. Bature told the court that he had received service of the processes on behalf of the governor. He requested an adjournment to enable him to properly brief Governor Yusuf and his legal team on the matter. The application for an adjournment was not opposed by the plaintiff. Speaking to journalists after the proceedings, Bature said he became aware of the case after hearing reports that a matter involving the governor had been filed before the court. He said: “Since the court fixed today for mention, I came to inform the court that I had not been able to brief him on the service I collected. He will have to decide on the next course of action.” However, the Kano State commissioner urged members of the public to exercise restraint in commenting on the matter, which he described as personal and sub judice. “This is a personal matter, so, I want to exercise some level of restraint because it concerns him personally and is also before the court. We do not want to overflog an issue that is already before the court. “We have to remain very neutral in issues like this because they involve families. There are many other stories that are newsworthy, rather than focusing on sensational issues like this,” he added. Zainab, who is the second wife of Governor Yusuf, is the adopted daughter of a former governor of the state and Vice Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso. She approached the court for the dissolution of the marriage, which produced six children, over “irreconcilable differences.” The plaintiff offered to refund the dowry that was paid on her by the governor. The divorce case comes amid a prolonged political fallout between Governor Yusuf and his former political mentor, Senator Kwankwaso, who was instrumental to his ascension to power. Governor Yusuf, while addressing pensioners at the Government House in Kano on Monday, confirmed his marital issues. The post Court adjourns divorce case of Gov Yusuf, wife to Dec 15 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Oracle reveals fix-this-ASAP-grade Java4Shell bug that allows attacks on many third-party apps
item.description: The United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has urged Java users to immediately patch a high-severity flaw in the software, which attackers can use to crash the Java virtual machine or achieve unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). Oracle revealed the flaw in its monthly patch dump for November , which offers 655 patches, 62 of them rated critical, affecting 62 products. Several of the flaws are rated more dangerous than the Java problem, CVE-2026-114938 , which Big Red didn’t single out as worthy of special attention despite CISA’s warning . The cyber-agency’s decision seems apt because vulnerability research and red teaming outfit Calif.io, which discovered the flaw, used its X account to claim news of the problem had leaked before public disclosure and the release of Oracle's fixes. By then, Calif had already tested the flaw, which it named “Java4Shell,” and found applications including Keycloak, Atlassian’s Jira and Confluence, Jenkins, Apache Kafka Broker, and Elasticsearch are susceptible to RCE. Calif, which also helped to find the PHP2Shell flaw , says the flaw is a memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. “Base64 is a very common way of representing binary data as text. It is used in authentication protocols, to encode file uploads, and to deliver network messages,” the company explained. “To decode Base64 faster, OpenJDK uses specialized x86-64 CPU instructions to process many bytes at once.” “We discovered a bug in that optimized machine-level code that lets malformed input overwrite neighboring memory. With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution. The corruption itself can be triggered by just 64 A characters followed by a single =:” Calif applied the CVSS 4.0 bug-rating scheme and gave the flaw a critical-rated score of 9.2/10. Infosec outfit SentinelOne’s analysis suggests the flaw “sits in the Java standard library, so exploit traffic is specific to each application.” “Any Base64 value an application passes to java.util.Base64.Decoder can carry the payload, including HTTP Basic credentials, SAML artifacts, CSRF tokens, and MIME encoded words. In default configurations of the affected applications listed above, attackers can reach this code path prior to authentication.” Cisco’s Talos security team pointed out that the flaw is present in OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled. “These vulnerabilities have already been tested against a suite of Java applications with success, but the attack surface is likely much larger as additional targets are tested and confirmed,” Talos advised. Cisco’s infosec experts urged adoption of the fixed versions of Java Oracle posted on Tuesday but noted it is possible to mitigate the flaw on x86-64 machines by starting the JVM with support for AVX-512 disabled. item.title: Courts must stop deciding election winners — Justice Adefope-Okojie
item.description: By Innocent Anaba LAGOS — FORMER Judge of the Court of Appeal, Justice Oludotun Adefope-Okojie, yesterday, warned Nigerian courts against installing candidates voters rejected through judicial rulings. She noted that “a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the electorate. They, in consequence, owe the electorate no duty to represent them. This is an aberration.” Justice Adefope-Okojie, who retired from the bench of the Court of Appeal in 2023, also cautioned political parties to comply with the tenets of justice and to observe their various party constitutions in their selection of candidates, to avoid such cases ending up in court. Speaking on the topic ‘Electoral Process in Nigeria: Managing the boundaries of judicial intervention,’ at the GAVEL International Annual Lecture, in Lagos, Justice Adefope-Okojie said: “The credibility of an electoral system depends not only on the conduct of elections but also on the existence of effective mechanisms for resolving disputes arising before, during, and after elections. “The ideal situation should be that the vote of the people should be decided at the polling unit, rather than the court of law. The contrary is, however, the prevalent situation in this country. The political parties have done immeasurable harm to the polity. “They seem incapable of abiding by their own party’s Constitution in their selection of the rightful candidates to be fielded in the election, which, contrarily, in a number of instances has boomeranged against them, with the rightfully elected but rejected candidate working for the opposing side in the actual election, out of spite. “The parties have also taken advantage of the courts’ position of not intervening in the domestic affairs of the party, to commit all manner of atrocities. “It is the flawed congresses and wrongful substitution of successful candidates by imposition of handpicked ones, and an electoral system challenged by honesty, that led to most of the litigations in the past elections. “At the actual election were accusations of ballot snatching, vote rigging, vote buying, manipulations and outright falsification of results. The resultant effect is the recourse to the courts for determination of the rightful candidate, a duty which should have been resolved at the polling booth and the rightful declaration by INEC. “The unfortunate result is that a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the electorate. They, in consequence, owe the electorate no duty to represent them. This is an aberration. “The simplistic answer to the avoidance or reduction of judicial intervention in electoral matters is for the parties to comply with the tenets of justice and to observe their various party constitutions in their selection of candidates. item.title: 2027: Don’t sacrifice Nigeria’s unity on altar of ambition, Jonathan warns politicians
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned political leaders against allowing their quest for power to tear apart Nigeria’s unity, cautioning that political intolerance, ethnic rivalry and electoral violence could plunge the country into crisis, ahead of the 2027 general elections. He expressed concern over the growing resort to political thuggery and the use of young people as instruments of violence. He also insisted that political competition must not become a threat to national cohesion and peaceful coexistence. Jonathan spoke at the third edition of the Peace and Security Conference, organised by the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja, with theme, ‘’Safeguarding Peace and Strengthening Social Cohesion in a Competitive Political Environment.’’ He warned: “We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and in our states.’’ The former President also raised concerns over controversies surrounding judicial pronouncements, particularly conflicting decisions by courts of coordinate jurisdiction, and warned that they could erode public confidence in the judiciary and encourage citizens to resort to self-help. “When citizens begin to lose faith in the courts and resort to self-help, the consequences can be disastrous. The descent from a loss of confidence in institutions to anarchy is a danger we must collectively prevent,” he said. He urged political actors to respect opposing views and recognise the legitimate right of others to contest for political power, while calling on Nigerians to prioritise competence, national interest and service over prejudice and personal ambition when choosing their leaders. In his remarks, chairman of Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, threatened legal action against political parties, candidates and their supporters who engaged in violence, intimidation and inflammatory campaigns ahead of the elections. Represented by National Commissioner, May Agbamuche-Mbu, the INEC chair said competitive politics naturally involved vigorous debate, sharp differences and passionate mobilisation, but warned that these must not degenerate into violence or lawlessness. He also cautioned against harassment, intimidation and physical attacks on INEC officials and ad hoc election workers, insisting that offenders would face legal consequences. He said: “I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation, or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff, or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences.” Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation, artificial intelligence-generated content, deepfake videos and cloned voices as

item.description: ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, and African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, were yesterday locked in verbal war over last weekend’s attack on the convoy of President Bola Tinubu in Abuja. While the APC-PCC accused the opposition African Democratic Congress ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, of sponsoring the hoodlums who pelted the President’s motorcade with stones, ADC-PCC challenged the ruling party to produce evidence that the opposition party sponsored the attack. In a statement, the spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Mr Dele Alake, said the opposition parties were arming young Nigerians and sending them to disrupt the party’s rallies. “To create the false narrative of citizens’ discontent against the President, the ADC and NDC now sponsor hoodlums, arm them with cudgels and banners, and commandeer them to chant ‘Bamaiyi’ at APC campaign rallies,” the statement said. It described the mosque incident as “the latest instance of this abhorrent and anti-democratic stunt,” adding that it amounted to “the desecration of an Abuja Mosque last Friday, where these thugs were mobilised to pelt the presidential motorcade with stones.” The council said it had seen it coming, adding that “hours before the flag-off of our presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on October 24, 2026, we alerted Nigerians to the plot by opposition elements to create undue tension, sow disharmony, and introduce violence into the campaigns across the country.’’ According to the statement, the opposition parties had perfected elaborate schemes to use deepfakes, artificial-intelligence-generated images, fake news, sponsored protests, and other forms of propaganda “to manipulate public opinion and spread lies about our nation, President Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress, and the processes leading to next year’s general elections.” “These unpatriotic and disingenuous plots by opposition elements have started unfolding. Their major objective is to deceive Nigerians and the international community by driving a narrative of discontent against President Tinubu”, the council said. It praised the security personnel attached to the presidential convoy for their maturity and for exercising utmost restraint in such a delicate situation. “We also commend the fatherly disposition of President Tinubu, who has since directed the Police Command in Abuja to release those detained for the infraction,” the statement said. item.title: Manufacturers urged to prioritise safety in paint production
item.description: Chemical and Allied Products PLC, CAP PLC, has said sustaining progress in eliminating lead paint in Nigeria will depend on manufacturers upholding established standards and working with regulators and other stakeholders to advance paint safety. CAP PLC received the Stakeholder Recognition Award for Contributions to Lead Paint Elimination in Nigeria in recognition of its transition to producing no-added-lead paints and its demonstrated compliance with the Standards Organisation of Nigeria’s, SON, limit of 90 parts per million of lead content. The award was presented by the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with Sustainable Research and Action for Environmental Development (SRADeV), under the aegis of the Lead Exposure Elimination Project (LEEP), during activities marking the 2026 International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week (ILPPW). The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of CAP PLC, Olalekan Aluko, said: “This recognition affirms the importance of the progress CAP PLC has made towards safer paint manufacturing. Responsible manufacturing goes beyond meeting regulatory requirements; it requires an understanding of the impact our products can have on people and the environment. We believe sustaining progress in eliminating lead paint in Nigeria will depend on manufacturers upholding these standards and working with regulators and other stakeholders to advance paint safety.” The post Manufacturers urged to prioritise safety in paint production appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ibom Seaport: All promises, no action
item.description: The Ibom Deep Seaport project is a depressing illustration of Nigeria’s penchant for recycling development promises without delivering results. Conceived in 1999 under the visionary administration of Governor Victor Attah as the Ibaka Deep Seaport and Industrial City, it has survived the regimes of Godswill Akpabio, Udom Emmanuel and the incumbent, Umo Eno, without progressing to actual construction. More than a quarter of a century later, it remains a political talking point rather than an economic reality. Successive governments have offered assurances, raised expectations and announced milestones. The late President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration reportedly secured the Federal Executive Council’s approval for the first phase in December 2020, which is a public-private partnership estimated to cost $4.6 billion and a preferred consortium involving Bolloré Africa Logistics and PowerChina. Yet, that approval did not translate into construction. President Bola Tinubu also promised the project during his 2023 presidential campaign in Uyo. His November 6, 2026 visit to Akwa Ibom, during which he again announced its approval, therefore sounds like a recycled promise. What happened to Buhari’s approval? Why was the preferred investor consortium unable to commence work? Were financing arrangements concluded? What exactly has Tinubu approved that was not approved in 2020? Where are the concession agreements, financial commitments, construction contracts and commencement dates? Nigerians deserve documentary answers. Enough of presidential declarations at political rallies. The reluctance of successive Federal Governments to activate this project is particularly troubling. Nigeria urgently needs to diversify its maritime infrastructure beyond the congested Lagos ports and the struggling facilities elsewhere. Ibom offers an exceptional opportunity. Its proposed deepwater facilities, with an approach channel exceeding 18 metres in depth, could accommodate large ocean-going vessels. Its container, bulk and liquid-cargo terminals, supported by a proposed 14,400-hectare industrial city, could transform regional commerce, manufacturing, agriculture and exports. The economic benefits are enormous: employment, foreign investment, expanded government revenue, cheaper logistics and improved access to international markets. Akwa Ibom could become a major maritime and industrial gateway serving the entire South-East, South-South, North Central, North East and neighbouring countries. Governor Eno must, however, move beyond political lobbying and demand an enforceable implementation timetable. Senate President Godswill Akpabio should deploy his influence to secure federal action. These senior Akwa Ibom politicians must make their prominent positions in the ruling party count. The President should publish the approvals, financing structure and contractual commitments behind his latest announcement. Meanwhile, government must proactively rehabilitate and develop other

item.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
item.description: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. item.title: Daily disruptive outages that ground planes and halt work – welcome to the new normal
item.description: Another day, another disruptive network outage (or two) as government officials and company execs scramble to assure an anxious populace that these are not coordinated cyberattacks – and security experts call this the new normal. A classified network that the US National Security Agency uses for internal communications, called NSANet, went offline on Tuesday in what the agency described as a “temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance.” “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues,” the NSA said in a statement following media reports about the outage. “NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.” Around the same time, Apple users began reporting issues across multiple services – including Apple Support, iCloud, the App Store, Apple Pay, and more – with Apple retail stores worldwide also reportedly experiencing disruptions that halted sales and in-person support. A day earlier, customers at major US banks including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and US Bank reported service outages that Chase attributed to “a software bug in on-premise hardware systems - there is no evidence this is cyber-related.” All of these high-profile outages followed last week’s US Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) order g rounding all planes on Friday due to problems with copper wiring during an L3Harris network upgrade, and a Microsoft 365 outage on Thursday. Redmond later blamed the massive service disruption on a faulty software update it pushed back in July. Despite the weekend respite from network outages, your humble vulture still had to field is-this-the-beginning-of-the-end questions from friends and family all day Saturday and Sunday, most of whom suspected Russia or China – maybe even Iran – caused the spate of downed systems and services. A highly sophisticated, coordinated nation-state hack would be a much more exciting cause for the disruptions. The real culprit, however, appears to be aging, under-funded infrastructure , riddled with decades-old bugs and held together by digital sticks and glue . “As someone who started out as a hacker , I know how tempting it is to connect the dots when major systems fail one after another,” Remedio CEO Tal Kollender told The Register, adding that there’s “no credible public evidence that these outages were part of a coordinated cyberattack,” and most have been attributed to technical failures. “What concerns me more is what these incidents reveal about the fragility of our digital infrastructure. We've built an interconnected world on layers of aging systems, complex configurations, and dependencies that organizations don't always fully understand. A single misconfiguration, failed update, or broken dependency can create disruption on a massive scale, even without an attacker,” Kollender said. “The uncomfor

item.title: GPU giants throw HPC users some tasty crumbs
item.description: At Supercomputing 2026 this week, Nvidia unveiled a new variant of its Rubin GPUs aimed at – you’ll never believe it – high performance computing (HPC). The creatively named Rubin HPC promises more than 50,000 CUDA cores, nearly twice that of the AI-focused version of the chip that Nvidia unveiled earlier this year. It will arrive sometime in 2028. According to Dan Ernst, Nvidia’s senior director of supercomputing, the new chip offers a rebalanced architecture optimized for the kinds of simulation, engineering, and high-performance analytics workloads common in the HPC and scientific computing communities. This is not the first time Nvidia has introduced specialized hardware. Last year, the company optimized its B300 accelerator for AI inferencing workloads. “Rubin HPC is the same idea,” Ernst told El Reg . “Within the Rubin platform, but we’re building variants to really focus on a specific sub domain of applications.” Details remain remarkably thin. Nvidia hasn’t disclosed peak performance memory capacity or bandwidth. That said, the chip will likely include features which show Nvidia can think beyond AI and still cares about the HPC community. Fearing that Nvidia could ignore HPC is reasonable becuase beginning with the launch of Blackwell Ultra (B300/GB300), the company traded double-precision matrix acceleration for higher throughput at lower-precisions. The result was a chip that at FP4 churned out 15 petaFLOPS of AI compute, but just 1.3 teraFLOPS at FP64. That's good for AI, but less useful for scientists. When Nvidia unveiled Rubin, it seemed the GPU-slinger would continue this trend. At 33 teraFLOPS, the chip was not only slower at FP64 than the Blackwell GPUs it replaced, but slower than Nvidia’s now four-year-old Hopper accelerators as well. Nvidia contended that for sparse vector-heavy workloads measured by the High Performance Conjugate Gradients (HPCG) benchmark, the higher ratio of memory bandwidth to compute should deliver meaningful performance gains. Meanwhile, for dense matrix-heavy workloads, for which benchmarks like High-Performance Linpack (HPL) are representative, Nvidia adopted a new strategy: FP64 emulation. We discussed the pros and cons of this technique in greater detail earlier this year, but in a nutshell it uses an algorithm derived from the so-called Ozaki Scheme. The algorithm works by decomposing FP64 matrix operations into a string of INT8 operations that, when run on Nvidia’s tensor cores, achieve higher-than-native performance. Nvidia, we’re told, isn’t using INT8, but it is unlocking substantial performance gains, at least for certain workloads. According to Nvidia, Rubin can churn out up to 200 emulated FP64 matrix teraFLOPS. While Ernst didn’t offer any specifics, he assured us that Nvidia’s HPC hardware should offer native FP64 matrix performance and customers won't have to rely entirely on emulation. Assessing the new chip's vector performance is much easier. With more than 50 thousand CUDA cores (by ou

item.title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
item.description: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA Launches Nuclear Power Systems Student Contest
item.description: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source. Some of the most interesting locations to study on our Moon face some of the harshest conditions. Nuclear power could sustain human life and allow researchers to study the resource-rich environment despite freezing temperatures, long nights, and deep craters that never see sunlight. “As NASA returns to the Moon and establishes a lunar base where astronauts will live, work, and explore, we need to build an infrastructure to make it all possible. Nuclear power could enable exploration in the permanently shadowed regions near the Moon’s South Pole, carry robust science payloads over long distances, and keep instruments warm through the lunar night,” said Carl Sandifer, a program manager for NASA’s Space Reactors Division at the agency’s headquarters in Washington. “NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge prepares the next generation of explorers to use the unique power within themselves to dream up a nuclear-powered Moon base of their own design. We cannot wait to see what they come up with!” Entries include a 200-word essay and an original illustration. Essays should describe one of the students’ unique powers that will help the mission. Illustrations should convey the students’ vision of a nuclear-powered lunar base that supports human and robotic exploration of the Moon’s surface using both radioisotope and fission-based power solutions and demonstrate the students’ understanding of the kinds of exploration nuclear energy can enable. Judges will review entries in three grade-level categories: K-4, 5-8, and 9-12. One grand prize winner from each grade category will receive a trip for two to NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland to learn about the people and technologies that enable NASA missions. Every student who submits an entry will receive a digital certificate and an invitation to a virtual event with NASA experts where they’ll learn about what energizes the NASA workforce to advance NASA’s missions and sustain America’s leadership in space. Judges Needed NASA and Future Engineers are seeking volunteers to help judge the thousands of contest entries anticipated from around the country. U.S. residents older than 18 who are interested in volunteering approximately three hours should register to judge at the Future Engineers website . item.title: Nvidia: ‘I’d Be Honoured To Return,’ Jensen Huang On Possible Reinstatement
item.description: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has said he would be willing to return to the position if the company’s board of directors considers his reinstatement to be in its best interest. Huang made the announcement in a statement posted on his X account on Tuesday, his first public comments since stepping down on November 12, following revelations about alleged extramarital affairs and concerns over his personal conduct. The former chief executive said he had received an outpouring of support from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers, with many urging him to return amid the company’s ongoing challenges. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Huang, however, acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected of the company’s leadership and expressed regret over the difficulties his actions had created for the board. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said. “I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” (FILES) Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia Corp., speaks during a news conference in Taipei on May 21, 2025. US tech giant Nvidia said on July 14 it will resume sales of its H20 artificial intelligence chips to China, after exports were halted due to US licensing curbs. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP) | I-Hwa Cheng / AFP His resignation followed reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving an executive of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US criminal investigation over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips in violation of American export controls. The allegations have also drawn attention to Nvidia’s role in the global artificial intelligence industry and concerns over the possible diversion of advanced US technology to China. The controversy has weighed on Nvidia’s shares, adding to uncertainty surrounding the company, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company. Huang’s possible return has attracted support from prominent figures in the technology industry, including billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk and other artificial intelligence investors. An online petition calling for his reinstatement has reportedly attracted more than 190,000 signatures. US President Donald Trump also expressed support for Huang’s return on Monday. The Nvidia co-founder has been an adviser to the president on artificial intelli

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
item.description: null Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer? It comes down to choices made for speed and science during the twin missions' nearly 50-year journey, specifically during the first bit when they were flying by planets. The result is Voyager 1 is zooming out at a speed of 3.5 Earth-sun distances (astronomical units a year), while Voyager 2 has a more stately speed of 3.1 Earth-sun distances, according to NASA . Need for speed The original aim of both the spacecraft, which launched about two weeks apart in 1977 with Voyager 2 going first, was to look at Jupiter and Saturn. If funding persisted, which it did, the hope was to bring Voyager 2 past Uranus and Neptune, taking advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Voyager 1, by contrast, made a turn at Saturn to look at the planet's rings and the prebiotic (pre-life-chemistry) moon of Titan , before flying outside the plane of the solar system. NASA had a range of trajectory options to consider when launching the spacecraft, and elected to bring Voyager 1 at a faster trajectory — as illustrated in this video by Britannica, where you can quickly see the spacecraft overtaking Voyager 2 on its way to Jupiter even though Voyager 1. Voyager 1 arrived at Jupiter on March 5, 1979 while Voyager 2 got there four months later on July 9. The trajectories of Voyager 1 and 2 through the outer solar system. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Each of the spacecraft then performed a "gravity assist"—a sort of slingshot around the planet in which they took a tiny bit of momentum from Jupiter to gain speed as the spacecraft flew to Saturn. This technique is used constantly, such as recently when the ESCAPADE Mars mission flew two spacecraft by Earth on the way to the Red Planet, as it allows spacecraft to gain speed while saving on fuel. The planets themselves don't slow down that much. "Because the planet is so much more massive than the spacecraft, the transfer doesn't affect the planet to any measurable extent, but to the spacecraft it's a big deal," the Planetary Society wrote . "For example, we can calculate that during the Voyager encounters with Jupiter in 1979, Jupiter slowed down by roughly 10 to the -24th power kilometers per second — a change much too small to measure." "But each Voyager gained about 10 km/s [6.2 miles/s], a pretty big number," the society continued about the Jupiter encounter. This was "enough to put them on a

item.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records
item.description: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records Two NASA Space Apps Challenge participants in Vilhena, Brazil work together during the annual hackathon on their project submission. NASA On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries. The challenge provides an opportunity for hands-on experience with NASA science, mobilizing an engaged global community of technologists and space science enthusiasts to answer questions that benefit humanity and drive exploration. Participants join events organized by local volunteers to work in teams and address one of the challenges and submit their project before the deadline. Projects are then judged to determine 10 global winners, to be announced in January. “The Space Apps Challenge invites people with many different skillsets to leverage NASA’s gold-standard datasets to address real challenges facing us here on Earth and in space,” said Amy Kaminski, engagement branch chief, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “We’re thrilled to see more than 180,000 people tackling these challenges and helping to accelerate our ability to find solutions.” One of the local winning teams from NASA Space Apps Challenge NYC pose with volunteer local lead Nate Cooper. NASA Challenges also feature data from 17 international space agency partners, all Artemis Accord signatories. This year’s space agency partners are: Angola National Space Programme Management Office (GGPEN), Bahrain Space Agency, Brazilian Space Agency (AEB), CSA (Canadian Space Agency), ESA (European Space Agency), ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), Italian Space Agency, JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), KASA (Korea AeroSpace Administration), Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Center of the United Arab Emirates, National Space Activities Commission of Argentina (CONAE), Nigeria’s National Space Research and Development Agency, Paraguayan Space Agency, Senegalese Space Studies Agency, Spanish Space Agency, Turkish Space Agency, and UK Space Agency. Three agencies, GGPEN, AEB, and CONAE, also wrote challenges this year. To learn more about NASA’s Space Apps Challenge, visit: spaceappschallenge.org Karen Fox / Jessica Hall Headquarters, Washington karen.c.fox@nasa.gov / jessica.hall@nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 17, 2026 Related Terms Open Science Explore More 4 min read NASA Welcomes All Ages, Experience Levels for Space Apps Challenge Article 1 month ago 4 min read NASA’s Prithvi Becomes First AI Geos

item.title: Presidential Election: We Were Blindsided In Lagos In 2023 – Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Raji Fashola, has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was caught off guard by its defeat in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election. That outcome is one he says the party is “working tooth and nail” to avoid in 2027. Speaking in an interview on Politics Today, Fashola said the APC never anticipated losing Lagos, the political base of President Bola Tinubu, to the Labour Party candidate Peter Obi. “We were blindsided in Lagos,” Fashola said on Tuesday during an interview on Politics Today. FILE PHOTO: Former Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola. The former governor, however, argued that the result reflected the growing maturity of Nigeria’s democracy rather than a collapse of the APC’s influence in Lagos. According to him, electoral victories and defeats are part of democratic competition, and political loyalties can shift over time depending on prevailing circumstances. Drawing a football analogy, Fashola said political parties, like football clubs, do not win every match and must constantly adapt to changing realities. “In an election, sometimes you can’t win everywhere. Most times, you can’t win everywhere,” he said. Fashola explained that in previous elections, the APC had strategically redirected its efforts to regions that were becoming more receptive to the party. He suggested that a similar approach would be adopted as the ruling party prepares for the next general election. “It remains to be seen whether, as happened in 2023, Lagos flipped, whether Lagos will flip back,” he said. “And we’re working tooth and nail to ensure that we take back what we lost.” Although he said the party was blindsided in the 2023 presidential election, Fashola dismissed suggestions that Tinubu had been politically “demystified” by the defeat, insisting that opponents underestimate the President at their own risk. He maintained that the APC remains focused on convincing voters that the reforms being implemented by the Tinubu administration deserve continuity beyond 2027. The former governor, who argued that President Tinubu deserves a second term, dismissed the ideas and plans being shared by opposition candidates. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform, growth, and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He also queried what he described as the opposition’s alternative message, asking, “What is the alternative message to what we are currently dealing with? What is the compelling message? Obi contested the 2023 presidential election, finishing third nationally behind APC candidate Tinubu and Atiku Abubakar under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). However, he defeated Tinubu in Lagos State, where he secured 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606. The APC has ruled the metropolitan state for 27 years. Tinubu, a former Lagos State governor, had enjoyed considerable pol
